brief:
Al Jazeera examined why truces in Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and Ukraine have repeatedly collapsed despite agreements intended to halt hostilities between warring parties. The analysis, produced by AJLabs, traced common patterns across the four separate conflicts where ceasefires failed to achieve their stated objectives of establishing lasting peace.

The examination explored structural and political obstacles behind ceasefire breakdowns, investigating how agreements negotiated to stop violence instead proved temporary pauses in prolonged conflicts. Negotiators in each case faced distinct challenges to sustaining truces once fighting resumed, according to the reporting, with factors ranging from political calculations to military incentives undermining adherence to terms.
dek: Gaza, Lebanon, Iran, Ukraine: four ceasefires, none that held. AJLabs on why truces keep collapsing.
title: Four ceasefires unravel as parties resume fighting across conflicts
